title: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely
lede: A US Commerce Department interim rule requires licences to ship AI chips and servers to any data center that may provide compute to firms in China or the rest of the embargoed D:5 group.

points: The rule targets remote access: companies in China, Russia, Iran, North Korea and 18 other countries renting compute abroad.
It covers data centers or networks above 12 million TPP, roughly the peak compute of 750 H100 or H200 chips.
Brokers and indirect access are included, operators must monitor customers' ownership, and existing operators have 90 days to get licences.
Shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil now need licences too, unless bound for US-based companies.
Commercial recommendation systems are exempt, and the Biden-era AI Diffusion Rule is formally rescinded.

sections.text: Cloud and GPU-rental providers outside the US now carry know-your-customer duties for large clusters, which could tighten access to rented compute for training large models.
